bluf: The defining factor this week is the collision between the US war on Iran and US domestic politics: Democrats won both chambers on November 3 and the Vice President publicly blamed the war. Washington struck Iranian targets near Hormuz on the eve of the vote and tankers keep burning near the strait, while talks run through Gulf mediators. In Europe, a wave of hoax bomb threats against flights fits the pattern of a Russian linked hybrid campaign, unattributed so far. Russia killed 42 people at a Ukrainian aid center days before US mediated talks on November 10 and 11. Cuba is under severe strain from the oil blockade and is detaining independent journalists. This is the baseline edition, so status changes are measured from here.
coverageNote: Baseline edition built in the evening from wire roundups and regional outlets. The headlines table lists leading coverage collected tonight, not print front pages; daily runs will pull front pages from the New York Times, Washington Post, Wall Street Journal, Financial Times, Miami Herald and El País where reachable.

discourse.summary: The post election information space is dominated by authentic domestic argument over why Republicans lost: the war (Vance's framing), replacement and fraud theories on the far right, and a visible break between some extremist networks and Trump. Foreign influence operations were active before the vote, and their likely next move is to reframe the result as American defeat and division. No coordinated campaign has yet been tied to the European bomb threats.

items.headline: Democrats win the House and Senate
items.summary: Democrats are projected to exceed 250 House seats and hold at least 54 Senate seats. Alaska (Peltola leads Sullivan by 637 votes) and Mississippi (Colom leads Hyde Smith by about 1,100) remain too close to call.

items.assessment: A public split on the war's political cost between the President and his likely 2028 successor is a meaningful signal for Iran policy.
items.headline: Vance blames the Iran war for the losses
items.summary: The Vice President wrote that the war was the reason Republicans lost. Trump acknowledged gas prices hurt but said he would go to war again.

items.headline: House leadership reshuffle
items.summary: Speaker Johnson will not seek to lead House Republicans. Scalise and Jordan are running for minority leader; Jeffries is running for speaker when Congress convenes January 3.

items.headline: US strikes near Hormuz on the eve of the midterms
items.summary: Limited US strikes hit around Qeshm, Hengam and Bandar Abbas. Iran's Supreme National Security Council head said the strait stays closed until US addresses its conditions: lifting the naval blockade, waiving oil sanctions and a ceasefire including Lebanon.

items.assessment: Iranian claims are graded C3 until confirmed; the Qatar incident is confirmed by UK sources.
items.headline: More tankers on fire east of Hormuz; tanker hit off Qatar
items.source: Dawn live updates; AP via US News
items.summary: Iranian state media reported two more tankers on fire. Separately, the British military said a tanker was struck by projectiles off Qatar.

items.headline: Iran's security chief meets Putin
items.summary: Mohsen Rezaei discussed regional issues in Moscow, and Iran says it will supply Russian gas to neighboring countries.

items.headline: Gaza and Yemen
items.summary: At least four Palestinians were killed in Gaza on November 5. In Yemen's Taiz, government forces say they repelled a Houthi attack; the UN says water production has halved and hospitals are short of fuel.

items.headline: Aid center strike toll reaches 42
items.summary: Russian bunker busting bombs hit a school used as an aid hub in Komyshuvakha, then the shelter where people took cover.

items.headline: Erdogan wants direct talks with Putin; Italy readies aid
items.summary: After talks with Zelenskyy, Erdogan said he wants to discuss ending the war with Putin. Italy is finalizing a new military aid package.

items.headline: Putin seizes Japan Tobacco's Russian operations; drone strike hits Ozon warehouse
items.summary: Moscow took control of JTI's Russian business. A drone strike set an Ozon warehouse ablaze in southern Russia.

sections.quietNote: Nothing significant located this cycle. Collection gap: Serbian and Kosovo outlets were not reviewed in depth for this edition.

items.headline: PLA activity rebounds after typhoon lull
items.summary: 85 sorties from October 26 to November 1, 47 into the ADIZ. On November 3 to 4: 22 sorties, 7 PLA Navy ships and 5 official ships.

items.headline: Beijing's AI enabled influence operations ahead of Taiwan's local elections
items.summary: Taiwanese officials report AI generated content and cyberattacks aimed at polarization and lower turnout before the November 28 vote.

items.headline: Vietnam comments on China and Laos military cooperation
items.summary: Hanoi said the cooperation should contribute to regional stability.

items.headline: Yoani Sánchez detained in Havana
items.summary: The 14ymedio founder was held about nine hours, the third detention of an independent journalist in Havana this week after Cubanet's Camila Acosta on Tuesday. The US condemned the arrests.

items.headline: Grid at about a third of demand
items.summary: The UNE forecast 958 MW available against 2,850 MW demand on November 2, with blackouts over 20 hours a day.

items.headline: Government reorganization takes effect November 9
items.summary: Law 186 cuts central state agencies from 27 to 21.

items.headline: Reported military mobilization
items.summary: CiberCuba reports Cuba mobilizing forces amid rising tensions with the US.

items.headline: Transition settling after contested runoff
items.summary: Lula won 51.8% to 48.2%. Flávio Bolsonaro's party acknowledged the result after his annulment call; Trump called it rigged.

items.headline: Colombia ends 'total peace'
items.summary: Congress passed President de la Espriella's bill: armed group members must disarm, identify fellow members, hand over recruited minors, surrender assets and reveal links to politicians to earn reduced sentences. Leaders face at least 10 years.

items.headline: Paraguay seizes bank tied to the president
items.summary: Central bank took over Ueno Bank after its capital fell below half the legal minimum; about 3 million accounts and public pension funds frozen.

items.headline: Poland arrests four over military supplies sent to Russia
items.summary: Part of a broader pattern of sabotage and procurement networks targeting the main aid route to Ukraine.

items.headline: Hoax bomb threats hit European aviation
items.summary: About ten flights threatened November 3 and four Prague bound planes November 5. The EU transport chief says it is too early to say whether they are linked.

items.headline: PRC influence operations target Taiwan's November 28 vote
items.summary: Officials cite AI generated content designed to polarize and depress turnout.

items.assessment: Expect this framing to be amplified across Iranian and Russian state outlets after the US midterm result.

items.summary: A statement attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei claims Iran's control of Hormuz shattered the myth of American invincibility.

items.headline: Supermarket refrigeration systems hacked across Europe
items.summary: Unidentified hackers shut down supermarket fridges in several countries the same week as the flight threats; analysts see a pattern of low cost disruption.

items.headline: October ransomware roundup
items.summary: October incidents included a ransomware attack that disrupted patient care and surgeries at University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center.

sections.quietNote: No significant FBI announcement located for November 5. Collection gap: FBI and DOJ press release feeds were not reachable through search this cycle.

items.headline: Israel detains journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh
items.summary: Police and Shin Bet arrested the Arab48 editor and +972 contributor in Jaffa; a court extended his detention. Rights groups call it part of a campaign against Palestinian journalists.

items.headline: Paraguay: Ueno Bank arrests
items.summary: Prosecutors ordered the arrest of eight people including the bank's president and CEO.

items.headline: Brazil: Banco Master case
items.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro is under investigation in the Banco Master case without formal charges, per MercoPress.

sections.quietNote: No new incident located. Context: Capitol Police investigated 14,938 threat cases against members in 2025, the third straight annual rise. Watch the run up to the January 3 swearing in.

items.headline: Bangladesh garment workers win wage concessions
items.summary: After five days of protests and clashes with police, a new wage board agreed to a revised pay scale from December. Workers seek about $242 a month.

items.headline: Greek students march for education funding
items.summary: Students marched in Athens demanding affordable housing and more state investment in education.

items.headline: Judge blocks deportations of Afghans to Afghanistan or Pakistan
items.summary: A federal judge in New York temporarily blocked the flights, which could have begun this week. Advocates warn of Taliban persecution of those who worked with US troops.

items.headline: Rep. Salazar: Hispanic vote punished deportation policy
items.summary: The Miami Republican said the Hispanic vote punished the indiscriminate deportation of Latino workers.

items.headline: UN ends Western Sahara mission after 35 years
items.summary: MINURSO ended when the Security Council failed to renew it. Russia vetoed a US draft backing Moroccan sovereignty; a rival Russian draft also failed.

items.headline: South Africa's ANC heading for worst local result
items.summary: With 28% counted, the ANC had about 32%. Full results expected Sunday.

items.headline: WHO approves trials of two new Ebola vaccines
items.summary: The outbreak, mostly in the DRC, has killed more than 5,300 since May and kills about half of those infected. Early results are hoped for in early 2027.

items.headline: Ultra processed foods and children's developing brains
items.summary: A new study suggests ultra processed foods may affect children's brain development in ways that encourage weight gain.

items.headline: Google to cut search for schools that reject AI
items.summary: Student accounts lose AI tools unless administrators enable them, and schools that refuse AI entirely lose Google Search for students. Former FTC chair Lina Khan called it coercion using a search monopoly.

items.headline: Europe bets €525 million on chip design startups
Supreme Court November sitting under way
items.summary: Arguments run November 2 to 10, including St. Mary Catholic Parish v. Roy (November 3) and Department of Labor v. Sun Valley Orchards (November 10).

items.headline: DeSantis on the GOP result
items.summary: The governor described the election as close to an extinction level event for Republicans in many parts of the country.

items.headline: Claim: Brazil's runoff was rigged
items.summary: Made by President Trump on October 26. Status: unsupported. Brazil's electoral court certified the count, and the losing candidate's own party acknowledged the result.

conspiracies.claim: The midterms were rigged through fake ballots and compromised machines
conspiracies.whereSpreading: X first, then other platforms. NewsGuard had logged 55 viral midterm claims by November 5, 26 about fraud, 29 of them starting on X.
conspiracies.origin: Recycled from 2020 narratives about Dominion and foreign made machines, plus new claims such as an FBI Houston raid that supposedly found fraudulent ballots on November 2.
conspiracies.whyBelieved: It offers a ready explanation for a loss, builds on years of repetition, and links real Election Day problems into a larger pattern.
conspiracies.caseFor: Believers point to real Election Day problems such as long lines and machine errors, documented individual cases of voter fraud, foreign made components in voting equipment, and distrust of mail ballots.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: FBI Houston said the claimed raid never happened. NewsGuard found no credible source for a supposed Dominion whistleblower. Individual fraud cases are prosecuted but have not been shown to change outcomes, and even prominent former election deniers largely conceded this time.
conspiracies.unknowns: Final counts in Alaska and Mississippi are still pending; a late shift there could revive claims.
conspiracies.watch: Whether any candidate in a close race refuses to concede.

sources.title: AP Fact Focus via US News

conspiracies.claim: Democrats won by importing foreigners and registering them to vote (Great Replacement framing)
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Prominent right wing accounts on X, Gab and Telegram in the 48 hours after the vote.
conspiracies.origin: The Great Replacement theory, recast to explain the election result.
conspiracies.whyBelieved: It explains a defeat as something done to voters rather than a choice they made, and taps into immigration anxiety already high during the deportation campaign.
conspiracies.caseFor: Supporters point to high immigration levels in recent years, a strong swing among Latino voters, and Democratic support for immigrant friendly policies.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: Noncitizens cannot legally vote in federal elections, and no evidence of mass noncitizen registration has been produced. Post election analysis, including CFR's, and statements by Vance and Trump tie the result to the Iran war, gas prices and cost of living. Rep. Salazar said Hispanic voters punished indiscriminate deportations, which points to citizens changing their votes.
conspiracies.unknowns: Voter file studies of exactly who switched sides will take months.
conspiracies.watch: This theory has motivated mass casualty attacks before. Watch for calls to violence and for targeting of immigrant communities and election workers.

conspiracies.claim: Ebola is a hoax, a Western bioweapon, or a scheme for aid groups to make money
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Community networks in eastern DRC, French language TikTok, and Western anti vaccine and supplement seller accounts.
conspiracies.origin: Long standing distrust from earlier outbreaks and conflict, plus lab origin and planned pandemic narratives that took off online after WHO's May 17 emergency declaration.
conspiracies.whyBelieved: Decades of conflict, distrust of government and foreign responders, and the fact that no approved vaccine existed for this Bundibugyo strain make official messaging easy to doubt.
conspiracies.caseFor: Believers cite the history of unethical foreign medical experiments in Africa, large aid budgets flowing into outbreak zones, the lack of an approved vaccine for this strain, and repeated outbreaks in the same regions.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: More than 5,300 people have died since May, mostly in the DRC, and the strain kills about half of those infected. Health workers have documented the cases, and rumors have led residents to burn treatment tents, including an MSF isolation tent in Mongbwalu, and to hide sick relatives.
conspiracies.unknowns: How the first human infection in this outbreak happened was not established in the reporting reviewed for this edition.
conspiracies.watch: Rumors about the two new vaccine trials, which are likely to become the next target.

sources.title: KAS: Health disinformation and the Ebola outbreak

conspiracies.claim: A scientist predicted the world ends on Friday, November 13, 2026
conspiracies.origin: A 1960 scientific paper on population growth whose model reached a mathematical infinity around that date.
conspiracies.whyBelieved: A specific date, a real scientific source and a Friday the 13th make it shareable, and it lands in a stressful news cycle.
conspiracies.caseFor: It does trace back to a real, peer reviewed paper that named the date.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: The paper used the date as a warning about unchecked population growth trends, not a prediction that the Earth would be destroyed, and no scientific body treats the date as meaningful.
conspiracies.watch: Scam and engagement bait pages using the date around November 13.
